subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded provider-normalized tool schema cache now, or defer this mitigation to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The repeated source-level work is clear, but the permanent boundary affects provider hook contracts, custom provider behavior, plugin metadata lifecycle, and the prepared-runtime roadmap.

options.title: Refresh the bounded cache
options.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR so known bundled normalizers can reuse cloned schema parameters while executable tool state is rebuilt per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the prepared-runtime migration carries enough provider/tool facts to remove repeated normalization without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live repro before implementation
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures current-main live Google/Gemini or heap proof showing the user-visible impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Refresh the bounded cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR so known bundled normalizers can reuse cloned schema parameters while executable tool state is rebuilt per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision intersects the prepared-runtime migration and provider/runtime boundary represented in the related maintainer tracker.
